newsitem.title: USA: Paragon sees Q2 hurt by low prices, start-up costs.
newsitem.headline: Paragon sees Q2 hurt by low prices, start-up costs.

text.p: Paragon Trade Brands Inc said Friday that lower diaper prices and higher feminine care start-up losses could weaken 1997 results, especially in the second quarter.

"Looking forward, we see lower pricing for our baby diaper products in an increasingly competitive environment. This, combined with the higher feminine care start-up losses, will impact 1997 earnings, particularly in the second quarter," said Bobby Abraham, Paragon chairman and chief executive.
During the first quarter ended March 30, the company earned $0.32 a share on sales of $135.6 million, compared to a loss of $0.05 a share on sales of $137.2 million a year earlier.
First quarter diaper business results were better than expected and generated earnings of $0.64 per share versus $0.47 for the first quarter of 1996.
Start-up costs of its feminine care products led to higher than expected losses of $0.28 a share.
Full-year feminine care losses will be a considerable drain on 1997 profits, the company said.

Paragon said it continues its investments to expand its product line, improve service and reduce costs. The company said it expects these efforts to improve 1998 earnings and generate long-term shareholder value.
Paragon is a leading manufacturer of disposable diapers, training pants and feminine care products.
